mode .  In this mode it prompts for the next command with the primary prompt ,
usually three greater-than signs ( >>> ); for continuation lines it prompts
with the secondary prompt , by default three dots ( ... ). The interpreter
prints a welcome message stating its version number and a copyright notice
before printing the first prompt: $ python3.13 Python 3.13 (default, April 4 2023, 09:25:04) [GCC 10.2.0] on linux Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information. >>> Continuation lines are needed when entering a multi-line construct. As an
example, take a look at this if statement: >>> the_world_is_flat = True >>> if the_world_is_flat : ... print ( "Be careful not to fall off!" ) ..
